abstract: Despite the important functional roles of single-stranded RNA molecules in a number of biological processes, relatively little is known about their conformational ensemble, especially in divalent cations. We use the coarse-grained Three Interaction Site model for RNA (TIS-RNA) to determine the structural changes in rA30, rA120, and rU30 as a function of Mg2+ concentration at a fixed monovalent concentration. The Mg2+-dependent excess ions around rA30 and rU30, obtained in simulations, are in good agreement with experiments. Importantly, the agreement between the simulated structure factor and measurements using small angle X-ray scattering is excellent both in the absence and presence of Mg2+. rA30 retains local helical order across the Mg2+ concentrations studied, including 0 mM, whereas rU30 remains disordered. The simulations lead to two predictions. (1) Both rA30 and rA120 populate two distinct states (one more compact than the other) as the Mg2+ concentration is increased. At high Mg2+ concentrations (30 mM), only the compact state survives in rA120, whereas in rA30 the extended and compact states coexist. (2) The compact states of both rA30 and rA120 are hairpin-like and are stabilized by non-neighboring stacking interactions. Such stacks are common in folded RNA structures, and we derived the associated parameters by analyzing more than 2,600 PDB structures. The predictions may be tested using single-molecule Forster resonance energy transfer (smFRET) experiments. Plausible implications of the results for Mg2+-induced phase separation are briefly outlined.

metadata.title: Length and Mg2+ dependent conformational changes in homopolymeric single-stranded RNA sequences

summary: Coarse-grained TIS-RNA simulations of homopolymeric ssRNA (rA30, rA120, rU30) show Mg2+-dependent conformational states and agree with SAXS and ion data.
title: Length and Mg2+ dependent conformational changes in homopolymeric single-stranded RNA sequences
